title: The Impact of Perioperative Gabapentin on Chronic Groin Pain After Inguinal Hernia Repair
brief_summary: A common source of morbidity after IHR is chronic groin pain(CGP), usually defined as pain lasting longer than 3 months. Gabapentin is an anticonvulsant that is also of benefit in the treatment of neuropathic pain. We propose a randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled study of the effect of gabapentin on CGP after IHR. Their pain will be assessed with a visual analogue scale. For those reporting pain, the need for pain medication, or other treatment, and the effect of pain on their quality of life will be recorded.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Male patients 18 years of age or older undergoing initial inguinal (bilateral or unilateral) hernia repair by any method (i.e. laparoscopic or open surgery)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Age less than 18 years of age, recurrent hernias, emergency operations, already taking gabapentin, allergy to gabapentin, pre-existing chronic pain or psychiatric disorder
condition: Peripheral Nerve Disorder Associated With Repair of Hernia
